title: Package name, Bundle ID & App ID
content:
## What are package names, bundle IDs and app IDs?

Every mobile app needs a unique identifier that distinguishes it from all other apps on the platform. These identifiers are platform-specific:

- **Android package name** — a reverse-domain-style string like `com.yourcompany.appname` that uniquely identifies your app on Google Play and Android devices.
- **iOS bundle ID** — a similar reverse-domain string (e.g. `com.yourcompany.appname`) that identifies your app in the App Store and across Apple's ecosystem.
- **App ID** — in Apple's developer portal, the bundle ID is registered as an "App ID" that controls entitlements, certificates and provisioning profiles.

Emergent automatically generates these identifiers for you during your first build or publish. You don't need to register them yourself — the platform handles provisioning and signing behind the scenes.

<Note title="Generated at first build">
The package name and bundle ID are created when you request your first mobile build or submit to an app store. Until that moment, they don't exist in the project.
</Note>

## Package name & bundle ID cannot change after first build

Once Emergent has published your first build (or submitted to an app store), the package name and bundle ID are **permanently locked** for that project. You cannot rename or change them later.

<Warning title="Plan your identifier before first publish">
Choose your app's name and branding carefully before triggering the first build. Changing the package name or bundle ID later requires creating an entirely new app listing in the stores — your existing installs, reviews and rankings will not transfer.
</Warning>

### Align integrations with the same identifier

Any third-party integration you configure — Apple Music APIs, Firebase services, OAuth providers, push notification certificates — must be registered using the **exact same** bundle ID or package name that Emergent generated.

If you register an Apple Music integration under `com.example.myapp` but your iOS bundle ID is `com.example.myapp2`, the integration will fail at runtime. Always verify that external dashboards (Apple Developer, Google Cloud Console, etc.) use the identifier Emergent assigned.

<Tip>
You can find your app's package name and bundle ID in the workspace under **Settings → Mobile** after the first build has completed.
</Tip>

## Native mobile apps do not require a domain

Unlike web apps, native iOS and Android applications do not need a custom domain to function. The app stores distribute your APK or IPA directly to users' devices; there is no URL to visit.

<Info title="No domain purchase required">
You can build, publish and distribute a mobile app on Emergent without buying or configuring a domain. If you later decide to add a companion website or [convert your app to web](/web-mobile-conversion-canonical), you can attach a [custom domain](/custom-domain) at that time.
</Info>

Universal links (iOS) and App Links (Android) *can* use a domain to deep-link into your app, but the app itself runs independently of any web address.
